projectDetails.name: Pi Network
projectDetails.description: Pi Network is a mobile-first cryptocurrency project that allows users to “mine” Pi tokens via a social trust graph while the network progresses toward full mainnet launch.

topRisks.content: Lack of continuous on-chain monitoring lets abnormal fund flows go undetected, increasing the risk of delayed incident response.
The lack of a structured Bug Bounty program reduces proactive vulnerability discovery, raising the risk that attackers find issues first.
Missing CCSS certification leaves crypto custody controls unvalidated, increasing the risk of undetected security gaps.

reviews.text: Pi Network is a mobile mining app for a cryptocurrency that claims to be user-friendly, launched in 2019. Users “mine” Pi on phones without energy consumption, but the mainnet is still delayed as of 2025. The team is from Stanford, but it’s criticized for being centralized. It has millions of users waiting for listings. Overall, it’s more of a social experiment than a functional crypto.

A crypto project that emerged in 2019 and claims that mining can be done with mobile devices (such as mobile phones). Users earn Pi daily by entering the phone and pressing the miner button on the installed Pi application. Currency is pi .  There are many factors that cause a lack of trust. When I look at the data and the story told, I can say that it does not give me any confidence.

I remember starting mining Pi tokens using my mobile. I always thought it was a scam and it was draining my battery, so I stopped doing it after a few months and then.. Boom, the token was airdropped for real. PI is a mobile-mining cryptocurrency that moved to public trading in Feb 2025, the project lets smartphone users “mine” PI for free. As of Nov 2025, Pi’s price seems stagnant around $0.24 after reaching an ATH of $2.98. Pi hasn’t matched the hype: People are using it a bit more, and some whales and a few merchants are slowly supporting it, but progress is very small. Token unlocks are influencing prices and many people still think Pi is not proven because, even though it has a lot of users, the token itself is not traded anywhere.

Pi Network is a layer 1 blockchain that aims to make crypto currency mining accessible to everyone with a mobile phone. Pi uses the Stella Consensus protocol consensus mechanism which relies on a security circle in order to secure the network. It was developed in 2019 by two Stanford PHD candidates. The network technology eliminates intensive energy needs for POW and high amounts of Staked tokens for PoS. In my opinion Pi Network provides an opportunity for third countries citizens to participate in securing the network which will help them to earn rewards. However, the concept of no liquidity, open/closed mainnet and price of the token is highly controversial.

When Pi Network first emerged, I was fascinated by the idea of mining crypto on your phone and saw millions of people join. But now it feels like it hasn’t delivered. There’s no real network or blockchain live, so it’s hard for me to trust it. It still seems more of a waiting game on vague promises than a useful currency.

I looked into Pi Network, a mobile driven crypto project that started back in 2019 with the promise of making mining easy for everyday users. Instead of using heavy hardware or complex setups, Pi lets people mine coins through a simple daily check- in on their phones, which helped it attract a massive global community over the years.
But despite the hype, the project is still in a long transition phase the open mainnet isn’t fully live, and many key functions remain controlled by the core team. The idea of accessible mining is great, but without clear transparency, real utility, or exchange listings, Pi Network currently sits more in the “wait and see” category rather than a fully developed crypto ecosystem.
